title: Thyroid Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. Full pathway: workup -> histology/subtype -> subtype-specific staging and risk stratification (tables) -> stage / biomarker / line-of-therapy-directed treatment arms with per-node checklists -> surveillance and recurrence/metastatic pathways. Treatment leaves route to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; agents without a dose protocol here (radioiodine, TSH-suppressive levothyroxine, lenvatinib/sorafenib, larotrectinib/entrectinib, cabozantinib/vandetanib) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. matchDisease:false because the subtypes carry different protocol diseaseId tags. Invents no dose/regimen/criterion. Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Thyroid Carcinoma; no proprietary content reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison), Thyroid Carcinoma. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols and their own evidence layers; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Post-operative recurrence-risk category (low / intermediate / high) is estimated from tumor size, extrathyroidal extension, resection completeness, vascular invasion, aggressive histology, nodal burden and post-op thyroglobulin. It drives extent of surgery, whether radioiodine is given, and the initial TSH target. Reassess dynamically at each follow-up (excellent / indeterminate / biochemically-incomplete / structurally-incomplete response).

b.text: Radioiodine (I-131) is used for remnant ablation, adjuvant treatment of residual microscopic disease, or therapy of iodine-avid metastases. Requires TSH stimulation (thyroid-hormone withdrawal or recombinant human TSH) and a low-iodine diet. Confirm iodine avidity on a diagnostic or post-therapy scan before relying on it in metastatic disease.

c.text: Selective RET inhibitors (selpercatinib, pralsetinib) are preferred for RET-mutant medullary and RET-fusion-positive differentiated thyroid cancer, with high response rates and better tolerability than multikinase inhibitors. Confirm the RET alteration on validated tissue or plasma NGS.

d.text: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is an oncologic emergency: secure the airway, obtain rapid BRAF V600E testing, and start systemic therapy without delay. BRAF V600E-mutant disease responds to dabrafenib plus trametinib (with consideration of subsequent surgery / an immune-checkpoint inhibitor); BRAF wild-type disease is managed on trial or with cytotoxic chemoradiation.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and diagnosis
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation of a thyroid nodule or biopsy-proven thyroid cancer before subtype-directed management.

bullets.label: History and neck exam
bullets.sub: compressive / voice symptoms, prior neck irradiation, family history of thyroid cancer or MEN2

bullets.label: Serum TSH; neck ultrasound of thyroid and central + lateral compartments
FNA of the nodule with Bethesda cytology category
bullets.sub: molecular testing (e.g. Afirma / ThyroSeq) for indeterminate Bethesda III-IV

bullets.label: Serum calcitonin and CEA if medullary carcinoma is suspected or before thyroid surgery per local practice
Laryngoscopy to document vocal-cord function if voice change or before reoperation
Cross-sectional imaging (contrast CT neck/chest) for bulky, fixed, substernal, or clinically aggressive disease
Confirm histologic subtype - it determines the entire pathway

nodes.name: Histology / subtype
nodes.title: Histologic subtype
nodes.description: Thyroid cancer subtype defines a distinct pathway. Choose the confirmed histology, or enter surveillance for a previously treated patient.

nodes.name: DTC staging workup
nodes.title: Differentiated: staging and molecular workup
nodes.description: Complete subtype-specific staging before assigning a recurrence-risk category.

bullets.label: Document AJCC TNM stage using patient age at diagnosis (age < 55 vs >= 55 markedly changes stage)
Neck ultrasound mapping of nodal compartments before surgery
Aggressive histology on path?
bullets.sub: tall-cell, hobnail, columnar, diffuse-sclerosing papillary, or widely-invasive / poorly-differentiated follicular raises risk

bullets.label: Molecular profiling of advanced or radioiodine-refractory disease
bullets.sub: BRAF, RAS, NTRK and RET fusions, TERT promoter - identifies targeted-therapy candidates

bullets.label: Baseline post-op thyroglobulin and anti-thyroglobulin antibody once healed

nodes.name: DTC risk / stage
nodes.title: Differentiated: recurrence-risk category
nodes.description: Assign a post-operative recurrence-risk category (or select advanced / metastatic disease). Risk drives extent of surgery, radioiodine use, and TSH target.

tables.title: Differentiated thyroid cancer - recurrence-risk category (illustrative)
rows: Intrathyroidal papillary <= 4 cm, N0/Nx or <= 5 micro-nodes, no aggressive histology or vascular invasion
Lobectomy or total thyroidectomy; radioiodine usually not needed; TSH low-normal
Microscopic extrathyroidal extension, aggressive histology, vascular invasion, or clinical N1
Total thyroidectomy; consider adjuvant radioiodine; mild TSH suppression
Gross extrathyroidal extension, incomplete resection, distant metastases, or high post-op thyroglobulin
Total thyroidectomy + therapeutic neck dissection; radioiodine; TSH suppression < 0.1

options.label: Papillary microcarcinoma (<= 1 cm, no adverse features)

nodes.name: Micropapillary
nodes.title: Papillary microcarcinoma: active surveillance or lobectomy
nodes.description: Very-low-risk papillary microcarcinoma; observation is a validated alternative to immediate surgery.
bullets: Active surveillance with serial ultrasound is appropriate for selected patients without nodal disease, extrathyroidal extension, or high-risk cytology
Lobectomy if the tumor grows, develops adverse features, or the patient prefers surgery
No radioiodine; TSH kept low-normal
Not suitable when adjacent to the trachea / recurrent laryngeal nerve or with aggressive histology
Enter differentiated-cancer surveillance

nodes.name: DTC locoregional recurrence
nodes.title: Locoregional recurrence: compartmental reoperation
nodes.description: Resectable locoregional recurrence without distant metastases.
bullets: Compartment-oriented therapeutic neck dissection of biopsy-proven recurrence (avoid repeated berry-picking)
Radioiodine if the recurrence is iodine-avid and not fully resected
External-beam radiation for unresectable or repeatedly recurrent disease
Consider active surveillance for small-volume, stable, non-threatening nodal disease
Re-enter surveillance; move to the advanced pathway if distant metastases appear

nodes.name: DTC low risk
nodes.title: Low-risk DTC: surgery, selective radioiodine
nodes.description: Surgery is definitive for most low-risk disease; radioiodine is generally not required.
bullets: Lobectomy for a unifocal intrathyroidal tumor <= 4 cm; total thyroidectomy if bilateral disease, patient preference, or to enable radioiodine / thyroglobulin monitoring
Active surveillance is reasonable for selected papillary microcarcinomas (<= 1 cm, no adverse features)
Radioiodine usually omitted
Levothyroxine to keep TSH low-normal (about 0.5 to 2.0 mIU/L) after lobectomy, or mild suppression after total thyroidectomy
Enter differentiated-cancer surveillance

nodes.name: DTC intermediate risk
nodes.title: Intermediate-risk DTC: total thyroidectomy, adjuvant radioiodine, TSH suppression
nodes.description: Total thyroidectomy with risk-adapted radioiodine and modest TSH suppression.
bullets: Total thyroidectomy; therapeutic central / lateral neck dissection for proven nodal disease
Consider adjuvant radioiodine after TSH stimulation and a low-iodine diet (activity individualized to risk)
TSH suppression to about 0.1 to 0.5 mIU/L, relaxed over time with an excellent response
Radioiodine has no dose protocol here - shown as guidance; nuclear-medicine arranges activity
Enter differentiated-cancer surveillance

nodes.name: DTC high risk
nodes.title: High-risk (M0) DTC: total thyroidectomy, radioiodine, deep TSH suppression
nodes.description: Aggressive locoregional disease without distant metastases.
bullets: Total thyroidectomy with therapeutic compartmental neck dissection; resect gross extrathyroidal disease where feasible
Adjuvant radioiodine after stimulation and a low-iodine diet
External-beam radiation for unresectable or recurrent locoregional disease not controlled by surgery / radioiodine
TSH suppression < 0.1 mIU/L while disease persists, balanced against cardiac / skeletal risk
Enter differentiated-cancer surveillance; escalate to the advanced pathway if radioiodine-refractory disease emerges

nodes.name: RAI status
nodes.title: Advanced DTC: radioiodine avidity
nodes.description: Distant metastatic differentiated disease is managed first by whether it concentrates radioiodine. Confirm avidity on a scan before relying on it.
bullets: Iodine-avid metastases can respond durably to repeated radioiodine
Radioiodine-refractory = no iodine uptake, progression despite uptake, or progression within ~12 months of a therapeutic dose

nodes.name: RAI-avid metastatic
nodes.title: RAI-avid metastatic DTC: radioiodine therapy
nodes.description: Iodine-avid distant metastases treated with therapeutic radioiodine and TSH suppression.
bullets: Therapeutic radioiodine after TSH stimulation and a low-iodine diet; repeat while disease remains avid and responding
TSH suppression < 0.1 mIU/L between treatments
Directed local therapy (surgery, external-beam radiation, or ablation) for symptomatic, dominant, or CNS / weight-bearing bone lesions
Bone-modifying agent for skeletal metastases
Re-evaluate avidity at progression; move to the refractory pathway if radioiodine stops working

nodes.name: Refractory biomarker
nodes.title: RAI-refractory DTC: actionable biomarker
nodes.description: In radioiodine-refractory progressive disease, a driver fusion changes first-line therapy from a multikinase inhibitor to a selective targeted agent.

nodes.name: NTRK fusion DTC
nodes.title: RAI-refractory, NTRK fusion: TRK inhibitor
nodes.description: NTRK-fusion-positive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer.
bullets: Larotrectinib or entrectinib (tissue-agnostic TRK inhibitor indication) - high, durable response rates
Confirm the NTRK fusion on validated NGS
No dedicated dose protocol here - shown as guidance; physician arranges the regimen
Continue TSH suppression; monitor for acquired resistance mutations

nodes.name: RET fusion DTC
nodes.title: RAI-refractory, RET fusion: selective RET inhibitor
nodes.description: RET-fusion-positive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer.
bullets: Selpercatinib (or pralsetinib) - selective RET inhibitor, preferred over multikinase inhibitors
Confirm the RET fusion on validated tissue or plasma NGS
Referenced dose protocol is the medullary-scoped selpercatinib protocol (same drug); physician confirms fit
Continue TSH suppression; monitor LFTs, blood pressure, QT, and hypersensitivity

nodes.name: RAI-refractory MKI
nodes.title: RAI-refractory, no target: lenvatinib / sorafenib
nodes.description: Progressive radioiodine-refractory disease without an actionable fusion.
bullets: Lenvatinib is the preferred multikinase inhibitor (higher response rate); sorafenib is an alternative
Reserve systemic therapy for progressive or symptomatic disease - indolent metastases can be observed
No dedicated dose protocol here - shown as guidance; manage hypertension, proteinuria, diarrhea, hand-foot skin reaction, and thromboembolic / bleeding risk
Cabozantinib is an option after progression on prior multikinase therapy
Continue TSH suppression; use directed local therapy for dominant lesions

nodes.name: DTC surveillance
nodes.title: Differentiated: surveillance and recurrence check
nodes.description: Longitudinal monitoring after definitive therapy; a rising thyroglobulin or new structural disease reopens the advanced pathway.
bullets: Serum thyroglobulin + anti-thyroglobulin antibody and neck ultrasound at intervals; assign a dynamic response category
Adjust the TSH target upward as the response becomes excellent; deepen suppression if disease persists
Rising thyroglobulin with negative imaging: consider a diagnostic radioiodine scan or FDG-PET (dedifferentiation)
Structural recurrence: surgery or directed local therapy for resectable disease; enter the advanced / radioiodine pathway for distant metastases
Monitor for over-suppression effects (atrial fibrillation, bone loss)

nodes.name: MTC workup
nodes.title: Medullary: workup and RET testing
nodes.description: Medullary carcinoma arises from calcitonin-producing C-cells and is RET-driven. Complete germline and biochemical workup before surgery.

tables.title: Medullary carcinoma - RET germline context (MEN2)
rows: Screen for pheochromocytoma and hyperparathyroidism; offer family cascade testing
No inherited syndrome; RET still drives targeted therapy in advanced disease

bullets.label: Serum calcitonin and CEA (baseline and for doubling-time later)
Germline RET testing in all; if positive, screen for pheochromocytoma (plasma/urine metanephrines) and hyperparathyroidism (calcium/PTH) BEFORE thyroid surgery
Neck ultrasound; cross-sectional imaging for high calcitonin (e.g. > 500 pg/mL) to detect distant metastases
Note: medullary carcinoma does not concentrate radioiodine and is not TSH-driven

nodes.name: MTC stage
nodes.title: Medullary: extent of disease
nodes.description: Choose localized resectable disease versus advanced / distant metastatic medullary carcinoma.

options.label: Germline RET carrier, no cancer yet (prophylactic)

nodes.name: MEN2 prophylactic
nodes.title: Germline RET carrier: prophylactic thyroidectomy
nodes.description: Risk-reducing surgery in an unaffected MEN2 carrier, timed by the specific RET mutation's aggressiveness.
bullets: Timing is mutation-driven: earliest infancy for the highest-risk MEN2B (RET M918T), early childhood for high-risk, later and calcitonin-guided for moderate-risk mutations
Screen for and treat pheochromocytoma before any surgery
Total thyroidectomy; add central neck dissection if calcitonin is elevated or nodes look abnormal
Levothyroxine replacement afterward; begin lifelong calcitonin surveillance
Offer cascade genetic testing to at-risk relatives

nodes.name: MTC localized
nodes.title: Localized MTC: total thyroidectomy + central neck dissection
nodes.description: Surgery is the only curative modality for medullary carcinoma.
bullets: Total thyroidectomy with prophylactic central (level VI) neck dissection; add lateral dissection for imaging or biochemical evidence of nodal disease
Treat any pheochromocytoma FIRST if present (avoid intra-operative crisis)
Levothyroxine for replacement only - no TSH suppression, no radioiodine (C-cells are not iodine-avid or TSH-driven)
External-beam radiation for high-risk unresectable neck disease
Enter medullary surveillance (calcitonin / CEA doubling-time)

nodes.name: MTC RET status
nodes.title: Advanced MTC: RET status
nodes.description: In progressive advanced medullary carcinoma, a RET alteration selects a selective RET inhibitor over a multikinase inhibitor.

nodes.name: MTC RET+
nodes.title: Advanced MTC, RET-mutant: selpercatinib
nodes.description: RET-mutant advanced / progressive medullary carcinoma.
bullets: Selpercatinib (or pralsetinib) - selective RET inhibitor, preferred first line for RET-mutant disease
Confirm the RET alteration on validated testing
Reserve for progressive or symptomatic disease; monitor LFTs, blood pressure, QT, hypersensitivity
Referenced dose protocol below

nodes.name: MTC RET WT
nodes.title: Advanced MTC, RET wild-type: multikinase inhibitor
nodes.description: Progressive advanced medullary carcinoma without a targetable RET alteration.
bullets: Cabozantinib or vandetanib (multikinase inhibitors) for progressive / symptomatic disease
No dedicated dose protocol here - shown as guidance; vandetanib requires QT / ECG monitoring, cabozantinib requires wound / GI-perforation and hemorrhage vigilance
Observe indolent, asymptomatic metastatic disease with calcitonin / CEA doubling-time
Directed local therapy and a bone-modifying agent for symptomatic or skeletal lesions
Enter medullary surveillance

nodes.name: MTC surveillance
nodes.title: Medullary: surveillance
nodes.description: Biochemical follow-up after medullary carcinoma therapy.
bullets: Serial calcitonin and CEA; a short doubling-time (< 6-12 months) predicts progression and worse survival
Neck ultrasound and cross-sectional imaging guided by calcitonin level and trend
Continue germline / familial screening and MEN2 comorbidity surveillance where relevant
Rising markers or new lesions: restage and enter the advanced medullary pathway

nodes.name: ATC workup
nodes.title: Anaplastic: emergent workup
nodes.description: Anaplastic carcinoma is rapidly lethal and an oncologic emergency. Move fast: airway, staging, and rapid mutation testing in parallel.

bullets.label: Airway assessment first
bullets.sub: laryngoscopy; involve airway surgery early; tracheostomy only if truly needed

bullets.label: Rapid BRAF V600E testing (IHC and/or molecular) - expedite, it changes first-line therapy
Broader NGS (NTRK, RET, MMR/MSI, PD-L1) alongside BRAF
Whole-body staging (CT neck/chest/abdomen + brain imaging); essentially all are AJCC stage IV
Establish goals of care early given prognosis; multidisciplinary tumor board

nodes.name: ATC resectability
nodes.title: Anaplastic: resectability / extent (AJCC stage IV)
nodes.description: Anaplastic disease is stratified by resectability and distant spread, which sets the local-therapy plan.

tables.title: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma - AJCC stage IV substages
rows: Gross extrathyroidal extension or nodal disease, often unresectable

nodes.name: ATC resectable
nodes.title: Resectable ATC: surgery + adjuvant chemoradiation
nodes.description: Complete resection followed by adjuvant therapy in the minority with resectable disease.
bullets: Total thyroidectomy with therapeutic neck dissection when a complete (R0/R1) resection is achievable without unacceptable morbidity
Adjuvant external-beam radiation, often concurrent with radiosensitizing chemotherapy (e.g. taxane +/- platinum)
If BRAF V600E positive, neoadjuvant dabrafenib + trametinib may convert borderline disease to resectable - see the BRAF arm
No dedicated cytotoxic protocol here for this indication - shown as guidance
Continue multidisciplinary care and goals-of-care discussion

nodes.name: ATC BRAF status
nodes.title: Unresectable ATC: BRAF V600E status
nodes.description: In unresectable / metastatic anaplastic disease, BRAF V600E status decides first-line systemic therapy.

nodes.name: ATC BRAF+
nodes.title: Unresectable ATC, BRAF V600E: dabrafenib + trametinib
nodes.description: BRAF V600E-mutant unresectable / metastatic anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.
bullets: Dabrafenib + trametinib (BRAF + MEK inhibition) - rapid responses; start without delay
Consider adding an immune-checkpoint inhibitor, and reassess for surgery / radiation if a good response converts the tumor to resectable
Monitor fever (dabrafenib), skin, cardiac (LVEF), and ocular toxicity
Referenced dose protocol below

nodes.name: ATC BRAF WT
nodes.title: Unresectable ATC, BRAF wild-type: chemoradiation / trial / immunotherapy
nodes.description: BRAF wild-type unresectable / metastatic anaplastic disease.
bullets: Clinical trial is strongly preferred where available
Chase other actionable drivers on NGS: NTRK fusion (TRK inhibitor), RET fusion (selective RET inhibitor), high TMB / MSI-H (checkpoint inhibitor)
Otherwise cytotoxic chemoradiation (taxane +/- platinum) for local control, or best supportive care per goals
No dedicated cytotoxic protocol here for this indication - shown as guidance
Early palliative care and airway / symptom management

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance
nodes.description: General follow-up entry for a previously treated patient; the cadence and markers depend on the original subtype.
bullets: Differentiated: thyroglobulin + antibody, neck ultrasound, dynamic response category; adjust TSH target
Medullary: calcitonin and CEA with doubling-time; imaging by level and trend
Anaplastic: short-interval clinical and cross-sectional imaging; symptom and airway monitoring
Any new biochemical or structural recurrence re-enters the matching subtype pathway
